title: Compatible bounded-above resolutions from a quotient-generating class
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $\mathcal P$ be a class of objects of $\mathcal A$ containing every zero object, stable under isomorphisms and finite biproducts, and such that every object $M$ admits an epimorphism $P\to M$ with $P\in\mathcal P$. Let $K$ be a $\mathbf Z$-indexed cochain complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define the good truncation $T_n=\tau_{\le n}K$ by $T_n^i=K^i$ for $i<n$, $T_n^n=\ker(d_K^n)$, and $T_n^i=0$ for $i>n$, with the differentials induced from $K$; write $j_n:T_n\to T_{n+1}$ for the canonical inclusion. There exist complexes $E_n$, morphisms $u_n:E_n\to E_{n+1}$ and termwise epimorphic quasi-isomorphisms $e_n:E_n\to T_n$, for all integers $n\ge1$, such that $e_{n+1}\circ u_n=j_n\circ e_n$ as morphisms of complexes. Each $E_n$ is bounded above (there is an integer $b_n$ with $E_n^i=0$ for $i>b_n$) and every term $E_n^i$ lies in $\mathcal P$. Moreover each $u_n^i$ is a split monomorphism and its cokernel lies in $\mathcal P$.

source.place: Tag 06XX, derived-lemma-special-direct-system (statement and proof, including the strictification of the homotopy square and final epicification).

proof.text: The homotopy category $K(\mathcal A)$ is triangulated with the cone triangles and shifts, and its localization $L:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ is exact, by [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. We use TR2 and TR3 with the meanings in [def-weil-triangulated-category].

For $n=1$, the complex $T_1$ vanishes above degree $1$. Apply [lem-sfb-subcategory-left-resolution] with $a=1$ to obtain $E_1\to T_1$, termwise epimorphic and a quasi-isomorphism, with all terms in $\mathcal P$ and $E_1^i=0$ for $i>1$.

source.place: Tag 06XX, derived-lemma-special-direct-system, initial resolution using Tag 05T7(1)

proof.text: Assume the finite system through $E_n\xrightarrow{e_n}T_n$ has been constructed with all asserted properties. Put $a=j_ne_n:E_n\to T_{n+1}$ and take the actual cone triangle $E_n\xrightarrow{a}T_{n+1}\to C\xrightarrow{\delta}E_n[1]$ of [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. By the cone formula [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $C^i=T_{n+1}^i\oplus E_n^{i+1}$, so $C$ vanishes above some integer $b$. Apply [lem-sfb-subcategory-left-resolution] with that $b$ to obtain $q:Q\to C$, a quasi-isomorphism, with $Q$ bounded above and all its terms in $\mathcal P$.

source.place: Tag 06XX, derived-lemma-special-direct-system, induction: the cone and its bounded-above resolution

proof.text: Write $c=\delta q:Q\to E_n[1]$ as a chain map and set $B=C(c)[-1]$, using the explicit cone of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $B^i=E_n^i\oplus Q^i$, and $d_B^i$ sends the two summands by $(d_{E_n}^i,0)$ and $(-c^i,d_Q^i)$. Rotate its distinguished cone triangle backwards twice (TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category], applied in [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]); the resulting triangle is $E_n\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{v}Q\xrightarrow{c}E_n[1]$, where $u$ is minus the first inclusion and $v$ is the second projection. Thus $u^i$ has retraction minus the first projection and cokernel $Q^i$. In particular $B$ is bounded above with terms in $\mathcal P$.

source.place: Tag 06XX, derived-lemma-special-direct-system, inductive triangle; explicit cone construction from Tag 0G6C, derived-lemma-improve-distinguished-triangle-homotopy, proof

proof.text: Rotate the triangles $E_n\to B\to Q\xrightarrow{c}E_n[1]$ and $E_n\xrightarrow{a}T_{n+1}\to C\xrightarrow{\delta}E_n[1]$ twice. Since $c=\delta q$, TR3 [def-weil-triangulated-category] applied to $q:Q\to C$ and $1:E_n[1]\to E_n[1]$ gives the third component; shifting it back gives $[f]:B\to T_{n+1}$ and a morphism of the original triangles $(1,[f],[q])$. Choose a chain representative $f$. Apply the exact localization of [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. The first and third components become isomorphisms, so the middle component $L([f])$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso]. Each cohomology functor factors through localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], hence every $H^i(f)$ is an isomorphism: $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06XX, derived-lemma-special-direct-system, morphism-of-triangles diagram and quasi-isomorphism conclusion; Tag 014A, derived-lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle

proof.text: The equality $[f][u]=[a]$ means there are maps $h^i:E_n^i\to T_{n+1}^{i-1}$ with $(fu-a)^i=d_T^{i-1}h^i+h^{i+1}d_{E_n}^i$. For the degreewise retraction $r^i:B^i\to E_n^i$ set $H^i=h^ir^i$ and $\widetilde f^i=f^i-d_T^{i-1}H^i-H^{i+1}d_B^i$. The equation $d^2=0$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] shows that $\widetilde f$ is a chain map. Since $r^iu^i=1$ and $d_Bu=ud_{E_n}$, substitution gives $\widetilde f u=a$ strictly. The correction vanishes on cohomology (on cycles it is a boundary), so $\widetilde f$ remains a quasi-isomorphism. Replace $f$ by $\widetilde f$. For $i<n$ the equality $f^iu^i=e_n^i$ makes $f^i$ epic; for $i>n+1$ its target is zero.

source.place: Tag 06XX, derived-lemma-special-direct-system, lifting the homotopy through the termwise split injection

proof.text: Choose an epimorphism $p:P\to K^n$ with $P\in\mathcal P$. Let $D$ be $P\xrightarrow{1}P$ in degrees $n,n+1$, zero elsewhere, and define $g:D\to T_{n+1}$ by $p$ and $d_K^np$ (the latter factors through $\ker d_K^{n+1}$ because $d_K^{n+1}d_K^n=0$). Then $g^n$ is epic and the image of $g^{n+1}$ is $\operatorname{im}d_K^n$. The quotient of $T_{n+1}^{n+1}=\ker d_K^{n+1}$ by this image is $H^{n+1}(T_{n+1})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The composite $\ker d_B^{n+1}\to H^{n+1}(B)\xrightarrow{H^{n+1}(f)}H^{n+1}(T_{n+1})$ is epic. Thus the images of $f^{n+1}$ and $g^{n+1}$ together generate $T_{n+1}^{n+1}$, so $[f,g]:B\oplus D\to T_{n+1}$ is epic in degree $n+1$, as well as in degree $n$ and all the other degrees already covered in step 6.

source.place: Tag 06XX, derived-lemma-special-direct-system, final paragraph: the two-term identity complex makes the last two components epic

proof.text: The differential $1_P$ makes $D$ acyclic: in degree $n$ the kernel is zero, and in degree $n+1$ the image is all of $P$. In the finite direct sum $B\oplus D$, kernels and images are the direct sums of the respective kernels and images, so $H^i(B\oplus D)=H^i(B)\oplus0$ and $H^i([f,g])=H^i(f)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Set $E_{n+1}=B\oplus D$, $e_{n+1}=[f,g]$, and $u_n=(u,0)$. This is a termwise epimorphic quasi-isomorphism with strict equality $e_{n+1}u_n=j_ne_n$. Its terms are finite biproducts of objects of $\mathcal P$; it is bounded above because $B$ is and $D$ vanishes above $n+1$. The transition has degreewise retraction $r\operatorname{pr}_B$ and cokernel $Q^i\oplus D^i\in\mathcal P$. All earlier maps are retained, so induction constructs the required system for every $n\ge1$.

source.place: Tag 06XX, derived-lemma-special-direct-system, final replacement and completion of the induction

Existing Mathlib leaves supply triangulation and the isomorphism criterion for morphisms of triangles after exact localization.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the compatible bounded-above stages used for the K-flat resolution in sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, Left derived functors and Derived adjunctions ("Choose a K-flat resolution P to K"), via lem-sfb-unbounded-kflat-resolution-existence. The proof follows Stacks 06XX without changing the blueprint route.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q107-c027378c9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks derived.tex at Tag 06XX (lemma-special-direct-system, lines 9213-9325, statement and full proof), Tag 05T7(1) (lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, 5301-5360) and Tag 0G6C (lemma-improve-distinguished-triangle-homotopy, 3458-3484). The item agrees with 06XX hypothesis by hypothesis. The one extra hypothesis, that P is stable under isomorphisms, is the convention that makes 'cokernel lies in P' meaningful, and the only user (the parent lem-sfb-unbounded-kflat-resolution-existence) applies the item to flat objects, which are stable under isomorphisms. I checked all eight steps. Steps 1-3: the cone C^i = T_{n+1}^i + E_n^{i+1} is bounded above and 05T7(1) applies. Step 4: I recomputed the signs; B = C(c)[-1] has differential with components (d_E,0) and (-c,d_Q), and the two backward rotations give (E_n,B,Q,-i[-1],p[-1],c), split with cokernel Q^i, as in 0G6C. Step 5: TR3 on the twice-rotated triangles uses the square dq = 1c, which holds by definition of c; after exact localization lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso (Mathlib isIso2_of_isIso13) makes L[f] invertible, and H^i factors through Q. Step 6: the corrected map f~ = f - (dH + Hd) with H = h r satisfies f~ u = a strictly, since r u = 1 and d_B u = u d_E; it is homotopic to f, so still a quasi-isomorphism, and it is epic below degree n. Step 7: the disk map g is a chain map, the image of g^{n+1} is im d_K^n, and surjectivity of H^{n+1}(f) covers degree n+1. Step 8: D is acyclic, e_{n+1} u_n = j_n e_n strictly, the terms and cokernels lie in P by finite biproducts, and the bound is max(b, n+1). The new node lem-sfb-subcategory-left-resolution is exactly 05T7(1). It is statement-only and self-contained, strictly smaller than the item, and passes small-case checks (K = 0, K = M[0]). Duplicate search: grep of the DAG for 05T7, 06XX and key words found only module-sheaf or flat specializations (lem-pc-flat-truncation-tower, lem-pc-flat-truncation-successor, lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement, lem-kun-bounded-flat-replacement), the dual 05T6 nodes and functorial-tower nodes; none is a duplicate. Mathlib has only the injective CM5a lemmas, projective resolutions and the functorial LeftResolution, so no Mathlib leaf. lean.statement: theorem subcategory_truncation_resolution_system {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] (P : C → Prop) (hzero : ∀ X : C, IsZero X → P X) (hiso : ∀ {X : C} {Y : C}, CategoryTheory.Iso X Y → P X → P Y) (hbiprod : ∀ {X : C} {Y : C}, P X → P Y → P (X ⊞ Y)) (hcover : ∀ X : C, ∃ (Y : C) (p : Y ⟶ X), P Y ∧ Epi p) (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) : ∃ (E : ℤ → CochainComplex C ℤ) (e : ∀ n : ℤ, E n ⟶ K.truncLE n) (u : ∀ n : ℤ, E n ⟶ E (n + 1)), (∀ n : ℤ, 1 ≤ n → u n ≫ e (n + 1) = e n ≫ subcategoryTruncationMap K n) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, 1 ≤ n → (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero ((E n).X i)) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, P ((E n).X i)) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Epi ((e n).f i)) ∧ QuasiIso (e n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, 1 ≤ n → (∀ i : ℤ, IsSplitMono ((u n).f i)) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, P (cokernel ((u n).f i))))
